note: Written by the build team on 2026-11-20 for the Day 2 gate (topic: frustration of contract, ICA s. 56). Every expected passage is an exact sentence from the official Contract Act or from the judgment text; a law expert must review the questions and expected passages before this becomes part of the gold set.

items.question: When does a contract to do an act become void because the act becomes impossible after the contract is made?
Is an agreement to do an act that is impossible in itself valid?
Must a promisor who knew the promised act was impossible compensate the promisee for the loss?
What happens to a contract contingent on an uncertain future event when that event becomes impossible?
What must a person do who received an advantage under an agreement that is later discovered to be void?
Does the word impossible in section 56 mean only physical or literal impossibility?

expect.contains: has not been used here in the sense of physical or literal impossibility

items.question: Is the doctrine of frustration part of section 56 of the Indian Contract Act?

expect.contains: We hold, therefore, that the doctrine of frustration is really an aspect

items.question: Does section 56 leave frustration to be decided according to the intention of the parties?

expect.contains: lays down a rule of positive law and does not leave the matter to be determined according to the intention of the parties

items.question: Was the agreement to sell land in Satyabrata Ghose frustrated by the requisition of the land?

expect.contains: the contract has not been frustrated at all

items.question: Is a contract discharged because its performance has become more onerous due to an unforeseen turn of events?

expect.contains: performance of the contract may become onerous. That is the law both in India and in England

items.question: Does a wholly abnormal rise in prices by itself affect the bargain the parties have made?

expect.contains: a wholly abnormal rise or fall in prices, a sudden depreciation of currency

items.question: Was the buyer's obligation to obtain an import licence absolute in the Naihati Jute Mills case?

expect.contains: the stipulation as to obtaining the import licence was absolute

items.question: When a force majeure event happens outside the terms of the contract, is frustration governed by section 32 or section 56?

expect.contains: If, however, frustration is to take place de hors the contract, it will be governed by Section 56

items.question: Does an unexpected rise in the price of coal excuse a power generator from performing its contract?

expect.contains: an unexpected rise in the price of coal will not absolve the generating companies from performing their part of the contract

items.question: Does a mere rise in price that makes a contract more expensive to perform amount to frustration?

expect.contains: a mere rise in price rendering the contract more expensive to perform does not constitute frustration
